Fragment intent, not gameplay vocabulary

Input

Abyssal uses generic Fragment input channels. The engine defines channels such as Input1 and Input2; Components decide what those channels mean.

Core Rule

Hardware, AI controllers, and authored producers can all provide input. Controllers translate their source into logical channels. Fragments consume those channels, and Components decide what each channel means.

Player Input Bindings

Player Profile Bindings translate physical controls into this Fragment's local input channels.

ChannelExample bindings
Input1MouseLeft, Gamepad0.Button0
Input2MouseRight, Gamepad0.Button1
Input3Space, Gamepad0.Button2
Input4ShiftLeft, Gamepad0.Button3

Bindings live on the Root Player profile because they describe how a player drives that Fragment. They are not shared Core definitions; an AI commander supplies its own logical channel values instead.

Use the picker beside Positive / Axis or Negative / Opposite to capture one keyboard key, mouse button, gamepad button, or physical stick direction. Each capture is appended to the field, so multiple controls can share a channel; press Escape while capturing to cancel. Stick captures include their signed direction, such as Gamepad0.LeftStickX+ or Gamepad0.LeftStickY-; non-standard axes use Gamepad0.AxisN+ or Gamepad0.AxisN-.

For complete binding instructions, mouse options, and supported control IDs, see Authored Mouse Flight and Supported Control IDs below.

Fragment Input Channels

Each Fragment has its own local channels from Input1 through Input10. Input1 on a fighter can fire a cannon while Input1 on a gate can activate the gate.

Multiple Components may listen to the same channel. Two muzzle Weapon Components can both use Input1, so one player action fires both weapons.

The channel number is local to the Fragment receiving it. It is not a global action name.

Authored Mouse Flight

Bind MouseX and MouseY to the local channels used by your Fragment’s Yaw and Pitch Components. Mouse axes are signed per-frame motion: MouseX is positive when moving left, and MouseY is positive when moving down. Put an axis in Positive / Axis by itself; use Negative / Opposite only for paired keys or buttons.

MouseX and MouseY are Player hardware controls. If Yaw or Pitch is authored in Root Core, that Component is shared, but AI and other commanders must provide the same logical channel values through their own input producer.

Player Profile optionWhat it does
Consume MouseWhile this Fragment is possessed, mouse motion drives its authored bindings instead of editor-camera look.
Hide Mouse (Pointer Lock)Requires Consume Mouse. Hides and locks the cursor so Mouse X/Y continue reporting after the physical cursor reaches a viewport edge.

Pointer lock is requested when Play begins. If a browser requires a direct gesture, click the Play viewport once to grant it. While the cursor is hidden, world-item selection is disabled so a flight click cannot select a Fragment accidentally; press F8 to jump to Wings Eye when you intentionally need editor selection. Press Escape to release the locked cursor. Stopping Play or releasing possession also restores the cursor.

Auto Input

Auto Input is an authored producer. When its conditions are met, it emits a local input channel at a configured rate, allowing existing Components to react without special-case combat code.

For example, Auto Input can emit Input1 while a target is in range. Any Weapon Component listening to Input1 may fire.

Auto Input can feed any Component that listens to the selected channel, including Weapon, Acceleration, Pitch, Yaw, Barrel Roll, and Respawn. The channel is the connection between the producer and those listeners; the listener decides what the signal means.

Auto Input is not a replacement for Player Input Bindings. It is another producer that speaks the same channel language.

Read the Auto Input component details and see the other component explanations.

Supported Control IDs

Use Gamepad0.Button0 through Gamepad0.Button16 for the first connected controller. Replace 0 after Gamepad to address another controller.

Keyboard controls are not limited to the examples below. Any standard browser KeyboardEvent.code can be entered manually in a binding field. Key(AnyKeyboardKey) is a description of the pattern, not a literal value to type.

ControlMeaning
KeyboardEvent.codeAny physical keyboard key, entered by its code; examples include KeyR, KeyF, Digit1, NumpadEnter, F1, BracketLeft, and Slash
MouseLeftLeft mouse button
MouseRightRight mouse button
MouseXSigned horizontal mouse motion: left is positive
MouseYSigned vertical mouse motion: down is positive
SpaceKeyboard Space
ShiftLeftKeyboard Left Shift
ControlLeftKeyboard Left Control
KeyEKeyboard E
KeyQKeyboard Q
Gamepad0.Button0South face button (A / Cross)
Gamepad0.Button1East face button (B / Circle)
Gamepad0.Button2West face button (X / Square)
Gamepad0.Button3North face button (Y / Triangle)
Gamepad0.Button4Left bumper (LB / L1)
Gamepad0.Button5Right bumper (RB / R1)
Gamepad0.Button6Left trigger (LT / L2)
Gamepad0.Button7Right trigger (RT / R2)
Gamepad0.Button8Back / View / Select
Gamepad0.Button9Start / Menu
Gamepad0.Button10Left stick press (L3)
Gamepad0.Button11Right stick press (R3)
Gamepad0.Button12D-pad up
Gamepad0.Button13D-pad down
Gamepad0.Button14D-pad left
Gamepad0.Button15D-pad right
Gamepad0.Button16Home / Guide (availability depends on browser and controller)
Gamepad0.LeftStickX+ / LeftStickX- / LeftStickY+ / LeftStickY-Left stick +X, -X, +Y, and -Y directions
Gamepad0.RightStickX+ / RightStickX- / RightStickY+ / RightStickY-Right stick +X, -X, +Y, and -Y directions

Mouse axes are normalized per-frame motion in the same signed range as a stick. A signed axis can be placed in Positive / Axis by itself, or capture its + and - directions into the matching fields. Physical gamepads and authored UI Virtual Joysticks use the same signed channel language, so a UI stick can drive the same +X, -X, +Y, and -Y bindings. The picker polls physical gamepads while it is capturing, so press a button or move a stick after opening it. Names follow the standard gamepad layout. A controller or browser may expose fewer buttons; a missing button simply has no input value.

Barrel Roll Inputs

The authored Barrel Roll Component uses one Input Channel, just like Pitch and Yaw. It can be authored in Root Core for a shared flight model or in a specific controller profile for unique behavior. In a Player Profile binding, put the positive control in Positive / Axis and an opposite key or button in Negative / Opposite. The binding combines those controls into one signed value: positive rolls one direction, negative rolls the opposite direction.

Holding the control continuously rolls the ship, and releasing it stops the roll. The Component's Sensitivity sets the roll rate; the default is 6 radians per second at full input.

Read the Barrel Roll component details.
